boundedDecisions: Use one 10000ms deadline across fetch and response-body read, with own Promise.race so an abort-ignoring body cannot hold the UI pending.
Abort and settle a prior read before the next invocation; clear its timer and only its own cancel handle. Preserve latest-request ownership.
Check monotonic expiry and abort both before body parsing and before accepting its result; refuse expired results even when timer delivery is delayed.
Failure uses existing accessible unavailable/retry state; no automatic retry or money navigation.
Retain synthetic ignored-abort race cases and independently verify native HTTP fetch/JSON abort and server-side closure inside a private loopback namespace.
limitations: Browser timer delivery depends on JavaScript scheduling. The elapsed-time guards also reject late completions; no background-suspension wall-time guarantee is claimed.
Browser test clock advances are controlled/simulated; transport, native fetch/Response.json/AbortController and server response closure are genuine isolated HTTP behavior.
Real Telegram/iOS/WebKit, human comprehension and actual screen-reader announcements remain unverified.
No server-side revision/cross-session freshness or backend money-execution acceptance is implied.
